text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000334 bills 99215 well above risk-adjusted expectation at every complexity tier, but with only three documented 99215 claims the records are too thin to say whether the excess is upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The 99215 share runs roughly two to four times the all-provider rate in every complexity band, including patients with zero or one condition. Sampled low-complexity 99215s such as C0185341 (urinary tract infection code only), C0185668 (rash) and C0185909 (abdominal pain) are the kind of visits where top-level billing is hard to explain, and the heavy concentration in 99214 also merits a look. Against that, the three documented 99215s (C0185746, C0186119, C0186121) all show high MDM, the panel does include genuinely complex patients such as C0185360 and C0185399, and the few data-reviewed-without-lab mismatches are weak evidence at most. Because records cover only a small share of claims and no low-complexity 99215 has been charted, the documentation cannot yet confirm or refute the statistical signal. A reviewer should first request charts for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed in the packet and check whether the documented MDM and time actually support level 5."}
